body.text: Classification follows NEI 18-04, endorsed by RG 1.233.
body.anchor: Safety classification of structures, systems, or components (SSCs) is performed in accordance with NEI 18-04

body.text: PRA Safety Functions are initially assigned to systems, and a structured approach identifies the SSCs that perform them.
body.anchor: Safety Functions are initially assigned to systems

body.text: The safety significance of a PRA Safety Function determines the classification of the SSCs credited to perform it.
body.anchor: The safety significance of a PRA Safety Function determines the safety classification

checks.q: What determines the safety classification of an SSC?
o: The safety significance of the PRA Safety Function it is credited to perform
checks.x: The safety significance of a PRA Safety Function determines the classification.
checks.anchor: The safety significance of a PRA Safety Function determines the safety classification

cells: PRA safety functions credited to keep the consequence of a DBE, or the frequency of a high-consequence BDBE, inside the F-C Target, and to conservatively ensure 10 CFR 50.34 dose requirements can be met
rows.anchor: credited to maintain the consequence of one or more design basis events

cells: Non-SR PSFs that are risk-significant or required for DID adequacy
rows.anchor: are the non-SR PSFs that are risk-significant or are required for defense-in-depth

cells: PSFs that are not SR or NSRST. They are not safety-significant and are not listed in Chapter 5
rows.anchor: NST functions are not safety-significant and are not listed in this chapter

body.text: An SSC is risk-significant if its function is needed to keep any LBE inside the F-C Target, or if the total frequency of LBEs with the SSC failed is within one percent of any of the three cumulative risk targets.
body.anchor: SSCs are classified as risk-significant if the SSC function is necessary to keep any LBEs inside the F-C Target

body.text: The term SR function is synonymous with required safety function in NEI 18-04.
body.anchor: The term SR function is synonymous with the term required safety function

checks.q: A non-SR function required for defense-in-depth adequacy is classified as what?
checks.x: NSRST functions are non-SR PSFs that are risk-significant or required for DID adequacy.
checks.anchor: are the non-SR PSFs that are risk-significant or are required for defense-in-depth

body.text: DL3-RC1 is scram by gravity driven absorber insertion by latch release.

items: CRD: releases the control rod assemblies on a scram signal from the RPS
RCC: control rod assemblies insert to a depth and within a time limit
RES: provides support and position control so rod release is uninhibited
RPS: generates a scram signal on exceeding a scram setpoint
body.anchor: Upon receipt of a scram signal from RPS

body.text: One SR function often spans several systems. When you study a system, ask which function it is credited for.

checks.q: In SR function DL3-RC1, what does the Reactor Enclosure System provide?
o: Structural support and position control so rod release is uninhibited
checks.x: RES provides structural support and position control preventing binding.
checks.anchor: RES shall provide structural support and position control

body.text: DBHLs specify the severity of hazards SR SSCs are designed to withstand with no adverse impact on their SR functions.
body.anchor: are a design specification of the level of severity or intensity of hazards

body.text: The design basis earthquake is the safe shutdown earthquake.
body.anchor: The design basis earthquake is the safe shutdown earthquake (SSE)

body.text: SR structures are located below grade, and they are damp-proofed and waterproofed to minimize groundwater intrusion.
body.anchor: SR structures are located below grade and are damp-proofed and waterproofed

body.text: Internal flood sources considered include sodium, molten salt, oil, and water systems.
body.anchor: flooding sources from sodium, molten salt, oil, and water systems

checks.q: What is the design basis earthquake?
checks.x: The design basis earthquake is the SSE.
checks.anchor: The design basis earthquake is the safe shutdown earthquake (SSE)

body.text: The SRDC are design criteria needed to fulfill the Required Functional Design Criteria for SSCs selected to perform SR functions.
body.anchor: The SRDC are design criteria that are necessary to fulfill the Required Functional Design Criteria

body.text: The Required Functional Design Criteria are compared to the Principal Design Criteria in Section 5.3 to confirm the PDC are complete.
body.anchor: are compared to the Principal Design Criteria (PDC) in Section 5.3

checks.x: SRDC are necessary to fulfill the Required Functional Design Criteria.
checks.anchor: The SRDC are design criteria that are necessary to fulfill the Required Functional Design Criteria

items: The failure does not cause the SSC to strike an SR SSC
The failure does not adversely impact an SR function
The SSC is analyzed and designed to prevent its failure under DBHL conditions
body.anchor: DBHL-related interactions between NSRST or NST SSCs and SR SSCs are prevented by at least one of the following criteria

checks.q: Which is an accepted way to prevent a DBHL interaction between an NST SSC and an SR SSC?
o: Design the NST SSC to prevent its failure under DBHL conditions
checks.x: One criterion is that the SSC is analyzed and designed to prevent its failure under DBHL conditions.
checks.anchor: is analyzed and designed to prevent its failure under DBHL conditions

summary.text: Classification comes from the safety significance of the PRA Safety Function.
summary.anchor: The safety significance of a PRA Safety Function determines the safety classification

summary.text: NSRST functions are non-SR but risk-significant or required for DID.
summary.anchor: are the non-SR PSFs that are risk-significant or are required for defense-in-depth

summary.text: DBHLs set the hazard severity SR SSCs must withstand.
summary.anchor: are a design specification of the level of severity or intensity of hazards

title: Safety Classification and Design Criteria
subject: safety classification

intro: Why is one system safety-related and another not? The classification depends on the function credited in the safety analysis.

objectives.text: Define SR, NSRST, and NST functions.
Describe the Safety Related Design Criteria.
